from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(MovingCameraScene, TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Digital currency faces a double spending problem.",
            "A shared ledger records all transactions securely.",
            "Transactions are organized into chronological blocks."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Digital Ledger", lecture_lines)
        
        # Visual assets
        ledger_text = Text("Digital Ledger", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        block_chain = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.6, color=BLUE) for _ in range(3)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        chain_links = VGroup(*[Line(block_chain[i].get_right(), block_chain[i+1].get_left(), color=WHITE) for i in range(2)])
        structure = VGroup(block_chain, chain_links)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in the text 'Digital Ledger'.
        self.place_at_grid(ledger_text, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(ledger_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Change text color to #FFFFFF.
        # Display a chain graphic connecting blocks.
        self.place_in_area(structure, 'C2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(structure))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight chain nodes with #FF5733.
        # Zoom out to show the full structure.
        self.play(
            *[obj.animate.set_color("#FF5733") for obj in block_chain],
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        self.play(self.camera.frame.animate.scale(1.2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Hash Function: The Digital Fingerprint", [
            "SHA-256 creates a unique digital fingerprint.",
            "Data transforms into a fixed-length hash.",
            "The one-way property prevents reversing data."

        hash_func = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Proof of Work: The Mathematical Puzzle", [
            "Mining is a difficult computational lottery.", 
            "Miners guess a nonce for valid hashes.", 
            "Successful guessing adds a new block."
        ])
        
        # Objects
        puzzle = MathTex(r"\text{Hash}( \text{Data} + \text{Nonce} ) < \text{Target}", color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(puzzle, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        robot = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg") if False else Square(color=WHITE) # Placeholder
        robot.set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(robot, "D3", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        new_block = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=1.0, color=WHITE)
        new_block_label = Text("New Block", font_size=18)
        new_block_group = VGroup(new_block, new_block_label)
        self.place_at_grid(new_block_group, "E5", scale_factor=0.5)
        new_block_group.set_opacity(0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(puzzle), Write(self.lecture[0]))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(robot), Write(self.lecture[1]))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        # Simulating computation
        self.play(robot.animate.set_color("#F1C40F"), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Write(self.lecture[2]))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))
        self.play(new_block_group.animate.set_opacity(1), run_time=1)
        self.play(new_block.animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Public-Key Cryptography: Digital Signatures", [
            "Users own a private key for signatures.",
            "Public keys verify ownership without revealing secrets.",
            "Cryptography ensures secure transaction validation."
        ])

        private_key = Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        private_label = Text("Private Key", font_size=18).next_to(private_key, DOWN)
        public_key = Square(side_length=0.6, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5)
        public_label = Text("Public Key", font_size=18).next_to(public_key, DOWN)
        
        message = Text("Message", font_size=20)
        signature = Text("Signature", font_size=20, color="#9B59B6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(private_key, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(private_label, 'B2')
        self.play(FadeIn(private_key), Write(private_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.place_at_grid(public_key, 'B5')
        self.place_at_grid(public_label, 'B5')
        self.play(FadeIn(public_key), Write(public_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        
        self.place_at_grid(message, 'E2')
        self.place_at_grid(signature, 'E5')
        
        self.play(Write(message))
        self.play(message.animate.set_color("#9B59B6"), FadeIn(signature))
        self.play(signature.animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        
        checkmark = Checkmark(color=GREEN).scale(0.5) if "Checkmark" in globals() else Tex(r"\checkmark", color=GREEN).scale(2)
        self.place_at_grid(checkmark, 'E5')
        self.play(Write(checkmark))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: Chain Integrity", [
            "Blocks link together using previous hashes.",
            "Changing any block breaks the entire chain.",
            "This design ensures total network integrity."
        ])

        # Setup blocks
        blocks = VGroup(*[RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=1.5, width=1.0, fill_opacity=0.5, color=BLUE) for _ in range(3)])
        for i, b in enumerate(blocks):
            self.place_at_grid(b, f"C{2+i}")
            label = Text(f"B{i+1}", font_size=20).move_to(b.get_center())
            self.add(b, label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        # Show connections
        arrows = VGroup(*[Arrow(blocks[i].get_right(), blocks[i+1].get_left(), buff=0.1) for i in range(2)])
        self.play(Create(arrows))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))
        tamper_circle = Circle(color="#E74C3C", radius=0.3).move_to(blocks[0].get_center())
        self.play(Create(tamper_circle))
        self.play(Indicate(blocks[1]), Indicate(blocks[2]), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        self.play(FadeOut(tamper_circle))
        self.play(blocks.animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Mathematical Foundations of Bitcoin: Trust through Cryptography
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic interest in computer science

sections.title: Introduction: The Digital Ledger
sections.content: Define the problem of 'Double Spending' in digital currency and introduce the ledger as an immutable sequence of data blocks.
sections.example: Imagine a digital 'magic notebook' where Alice gives Bob a token; everyone in the room must agree that Alice had the token before the transaction is recorded.

sections.title: The Hash Function: The Digital Fingerprint
sections.content: Explain SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm). Focus on the 'one-way' property: it is easy to compute a fingerprint from data, but impossible to recreate data from the fingerprint.
sections.example: Visual: A blender turning a bowl of fruit (data) into a smoothie (hash). You can't turn the smoothie back into the original fruit.

sections.title: Proof of Work: The Mathematical Puzzle
sections.content: Introduce 'Mining' as finding a 'nonce' (number used once) that, when combined with transaction data, results in a hash starting with a specific number of zeros. This requires immense computational trial-and-error.
sections.example: Visual: A digital lottery where 1,000 robots are trying to guess a 6-digit combination. The first one to guess it gets to write the next page in the ledger.

sections.title: Public-Key Cryptography: Digital Signatures
sections.content: Prerequisite: Modulo arithmetic. Explain how users prove ownership using a Private Key (a secret number) and a Public Key (a derived coordinate on an Elliptic Curve).
sections.example: Visual: A 'lock and key' animation where Alice uses her private key to sign a transaction, and the network uses her public key to verify it without ever seeing the secret private key.

sections.title: Synthesis: Chain Integrity
sections.content: Explain how each block contains the hash of the previous block, creating an unbreakable chain. Changing one digit in block 1 changes its hash, breaking the link to all subsequent blocks.
sections.example: Visual: A row of falling dominoes. Each domino is etched with the 'fingerprint' of the one before it. If you move one, the whole sequence collapses and alerts the network.
